title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GWEN'S DRIVE-IN
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gwen Soto, a DMV clerk in Kearney, Nebraska.
For twenty-two years, she told people to take a number.
Then she heard the town's old drive-in would become a storage yard.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN
segments.quote: I've been absolutely terrified every moment of my life and I've never let it keep me from a single thing that I wanted to do.
segments.author: Georgia O'Keeffe
lines: Old Vern, the owner, was done. Gwen had her savings, and a nervous stomach.
On her desk sat a postcard with a line from the painter Georgia O'Keeffe:
I've been absolutely terrified every moment of my life and I've never let it keep me from a single thing that I wanted to do.
She signed with a shaking hand, then sat down on a bucket of popcorn salt.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: ELEVEN CARS
segments.quote: Failure is instructive. The person who really thinks learns quite as much from his failures as from his successes.
segments.author: John Dewey
lines: Opening night, eleven cars came. The projector died. The popcorn burned.
Her sister texted a line from the philosopher John Dewey:
Failure is instructive. The person who really thinks learns quite as much from his failures as from his successes.
So Gwen wrote down eleven problems, and fixed them one by one.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE LONG NIGHT
segments.quote: Drama is life with the dull bits cut out.
segments.author: Alfred Hitchcock
lines: But people kept leaving early. A trucker told her, Lady, your raffle is longer than the movie.
Vern pointed at an old clipping in the booth, from Alfred Hitchcock:
Drama is life with the dull bits cut out.
She cut the raffle and the ads. Her speech became, Hi, popcorn's hot. The lot filled up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE STORM
segments.quote: Not for ourselves alone are we born.
segments.author: Cicero
lines: In June, a big wind ripped the screen in half.
Next morning, pickups lined up at the gate. Welders, ranchers, a whole bowling league.
Old Mrs. Novak handed her a hammer and quoted Cicero, the Roman:
Not for ourselves alone are we born.
Gwen stopped saying sorry and passed out gloves. The screen was up by the Fourth of July.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE FEUD
segments.quote: For me, the movies are like a machine that generates empathy.
segments.author: Roger Ebert
lines: Dell and Roy, two ranchers, had fought over a fence for twenty years.
One night they parked side by side by accident. Both cried at the ending. Both blamed the dust.
Gwen thought of the movie critic Roger Ebert:
For me, the movies are like a machine that generates empathy.
So Tuesdays, popcorn is free if you park beside someone you're not speaking to. That fence got fixed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE FRONT ROW
segments.quote: Everything in life is somewhere else, and you get there in a car.
segments.author: E. B. White
lines: That fall, Vern had to give up his truck, and he stayed home.
He'd read her a line once, from E. B. White, the essay writer:
Everything in life is somewhere else, and you get there in a car.
So every Friday, Gwen picks him up. Front row. Extra butter.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Do it scared. Learn from it. Cut the dull parts. Accept help. Park close. Go pick someone up.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Do it scared. Learn from the flop. Cut the dull parts. Accept help. Park close. Go pick someone up.
I went to a drive-in once and backed over the speaker pole. Now I walk in.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
